original_card.question: Can the 64-per-call centre path (eight rank-8 COPY/ERASE totals through the private temporary) be shared across calls or shrunk?
methods: Derive a fully charged favorable relaxation for sharing one centre path across k calls, including restoration, hosting and precision.
Prove a lower bound on copied information per call for the selected decoder contract.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show the changed centre charge and copy profile per call with every added restoration or hosting cost charged, and its ceiling via ceiling.ceiling(centre=...).

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write the per-call centre charge and copy children for sharing across k = 2 calls, charge the sharing overhead, and screen it; stop this route if even the ideal sharing gains under 10%. Ideal budgets: free 2.80x, shared by two 1.90x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The centre path consumes 64 of about 99.6 unpaid coordinates per call, i.e. about 64% of the raw deficit.
allowed_variations: One sharing pattern across a fixed number of calls.
One reduced copied-total contract for the existing decoder.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Removing copies without a replacement contract for the decoder's copied totals.

actual_scope: Isometric, free-conversion case of PR1714 open question 3 for k=2, C=I_2: in PR1714's root-code, separate-total union-price model, re-chart call 2's labels by phi in O(V,b) (free conversions). Do pure cross-call terms of rank < 8 appear, and can the two-call batch go below 128? Secondary: general cross forms in a V(+)V model (sufficient condition only; Corollary B' covers every invertible chart in that reading). Legal maps with priced conversions are not supplied.
scope_change_reason: Same card method (lower bound on copied information per call), narrowed to the one premise PR1714 names as material and leaves open: the common cross-call label chart. The question matters because the ideal two-call centre-sharing lever (128 -> 64) needs some change of PR1714's premises; this package prices the chart premise.
bottleneck_link: The centre path is 64 of ~99.6 unpaid coordinates per call; PR1714 closed root-code scalar sharing under one common chart. This package shows that changing the cross-call chart by an isometry, even with free conversions, cannot lower the two-call bill below 128, although rank-7 cross terms do appear.
stop_rule: Stop at 2026-10-15T04:19:33Z; package the rank-7 finding plus the scoped bound if the proof is not checked, or an exact isometric-chart k=2 decoder of cost <= 127 if one appears. At most one evidence-driven pivot (none used).
evidence: verify.py (exact F2/integer/Gaussian-integer arithmetic): independent P112 construction cross-checked against research/p112-single-lift/reference-geometry.json; 511-functional support premise; all 255 isotropic transvections and a 162-chart fixed-seed sample of O(V,b); 1,600 direct pure-cross ranks; five exact all-pairs decoders (250,880 entries); cross-form model checks; seven negative controls (isometry controls use an invertible non-isometric shear). PROOF.md: Theorem A (isometric charts, min 128, equality only without pure cross terms), Proposition B (c01+c10>=8 sufficient) and Corollary B' (every invertible chart in the V(+)V reading; any cross forms with rank sum >= 12), Proposition C (beta=0), Proposition D (any cross forms: total >= 128 - sum_double min(8, rho01+rho10) + sum_pure price; necessary conditions for sub-128).

ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance from Claude (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5): proof drafting, verifier code, controls and documentation, directed and submitted by thakrarsagar. Not human peer review or a formal proof.

open_questions.question: Is the k=2 root-code minimum 128 for every general cross form (beta01, beta10) in the V(+)V model, or does some form admit an exact decoder of cost <= 127?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Proposition B only covers c01+c10>=8 and beta=0; a sub-128 form would locate exactly which cross-call pairing a sharing interface must realize (and then price).
open_questions.first_step: Use Proposition D's necessary conditions (pure terms in both directions; double terms whose cross-form ranks exceed pure payments) to search low-rank cross forms against non-coordinate decoders with mixed spans, replaying exact all-pairs identities with this verifier's pricing.
open_questions.blocked_by: No mechanism yet; any hit is a model-sharpness control only until a legal, priced cross-call delivery interface realizes the form.

open_questions.question: Does Theorem A extend to k >= 3 independent calls with per-call isometric charts?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Batching more calls is the natural sharing route; the two-call Schur count does not directly generalize.
open_questions.first_step: Generalize count (2) to block matrices I - R with zero diagonal blocks and bound rank via pure-term ranks; test k=3 coordinate fixtures.
open_questions.blocked_by: A rank inequality for I - R with several off-diagonal blocks matching the per-term price floor 7.

open_questions.question: Do non-isometric charts in the single-V reading (call 2's own pairing changes), with an explicitly priced change of call 2's own demand pricing, help?
open_questions.why_it_matters: In the single-V reading non-isometric charts change call 2's within-call pairing, so they are outside this model (their V(+)V reading is covered by Corollary B'); they could only matter with a new demand contract.
open_questions.first_step: Specify the changed within-call price and recheck the pair lemma (P) for it.
open_questions.blocked_by: A legal interface for the changed demand; no free relabelling is admitted (PR1714 OQ3).
